profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a financial-services firm preparing a cross-functional executive briefing titled "Cryptocurrencies and the Future of Money" for the firm's treasury, payments, and strategy leaders. The briefing combines a research note on pure-asset coins, stablecoins, and central bank digital currencies with a handoff from the market-structure team to the corporate strategy team, which will turn it into executive-ready slides. The immediate agenda is to align on what materials will be handed over by Thursday, which version of the draft deck is the shared baseline, how the balance-sheet examples will be packaged, and what counts as the briefing being "ready" for the executive prep meeting on Monday. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on deliverables, handoffs, and ownership of the shared deck and appendix.

members.name: Alicia Romero
members.expertise: Crypto market structure, monetary economics, and institutional research writing
members.background: Alicia leads the firm's digital-assets research stream and previously worked in sell-side macro research covering payment systems and central bank policy.
members.private_state: She wants to preserve the analytical nuance of the research note, avoid last-minute rewrites, and make sure her team is not pulled into polishing presentation visuals over the weekend.
hidden_assumptions: When people ask for the "deck," they mean the latest research deck in the research team's workspace, currently version 12 with tracked edits accepted but appendix charts still being cleaned up.
A "ready" executive briefing means the analysis is substantively locked and all claims have internal sourcing, even if formatting and speaker notes are still rough.
The balance-sheet "examples" are supporting appendix items rather than core-slide content unless someone explicitly says they need them in the main narrative.
If strategy is "taking the deck forward," they will duplicate the file into their own presentation format after research hands over the content, not edit directly in the research master.
The Monday executive prep uses New York business-day timing, so a Thursday handoff means by end of day Eastern time.

members.name: Daniel Wu
members.role: Corporate Strategy Manager, Payments and Emerging Platforms
members.expertise: Executive communications, cross-business coordination, and strategic framing for new payment technologies
members.background: Daniel coordinates briefing materials for senior leadership and previously worked in management consulting on fintech and payments strategy.
members.private_state: He wants a clean, presentation-ready story for executives, avoid appearing unprepared in Monday's prep, and minimize the amount of rework his small strategy team has to do on Friday.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the "deck," they mean the executive-briefing file in the shared strategy folder, currently version 9 with the latest title page and message-map structure.
A "ready" briefing means visually polished, speaker-ready slides with a short takeaway on each page and no unresolved placeholders.
The balance-sheet "examples" are essential teaching devices that should be built into the core slides, because executives will not read a technical appendix.
If research is handing off content, both teams will continue working in the same shared deck so comments and edits stay visible in one place.
A Thursday handoff for a Monday prep effectively means available by Thursday afternoon so his team can refine the deck on Friday.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They repeatedly mention "the deck" and "the latest version" as if they are referencing the same file.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Alicia means the research team's master draft deck, version 12, stored in the research workspace and containing the most current analytical content.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the strategy team's executive-briefing deck, version 9, stored in the shared strategy folder and containing the current narrative structure for leadership.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both files have near-identical titles, both have circulated recently, and in coordination meetings people commonly say "the deck" without restating the folder path or version number because doing so feels overly procedural.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the material should be "ready for Monday" and that Thursday is the handoff point.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Alicia believes "ready" means analytically complete enough for internal review: claims validated, taxonomy settled, and appendix evidence attached, even if design cleanup happens later.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel believes "ready" means executive-presentable: concise headlines, polished formatting, and no visible gaps before Monday's prep discussion.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In firms with separate content and strategy functions, both standards are individually reasonable, so the phrase "ready" feels shared even though each person silently applies a different completion threshold.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on including "the balance-sheet examples" for Bitcoin, stablecoins, and CBDCs.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Alicia assumes this means a compact technical appendix with three worked examples showing liabilities, reserves, and asset backing mechanics, referenced briefly from the main deck.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes this means simplifying those examples into the main storyline slides so executives can use them as the core explanation of the categories.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see the examples as important and use the same phrase, but whether something lives in the appendix or the core narrative is usually treated as a packaging detail, not a strategic disagreement worth pausing on.

misalignment_points.topic: How the handoff will be executed
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that research will "hand over" the material on Thursday and strategy will "take it forward."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Alicia assumes her team will send a finalized content package, after which Daniel's team will copy material into their own executive template and own downstream edits.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes both teams will continue co-editing the same shared file after Thursday, with research available to revise wording directly in place as comments come in.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase "take it forward" is standard coordination shorthand that masks operational details, and neither side wants to sound territorial about document ownership in a cooperative planning meeting.

turns.inner_thought: We should keep this tight. Research is on track on our master draft, version 12, and I want to make sure Thursday still means end of day New York so my team can finish the appendix cleanup without getting dragged into slide-polish mode. If I frame it as a standard handoff, Daniel can take it forward in his team's format afterward.
turns.utterance: From the research side, we're on track. I just want to confirm we're still working to a Thursday handoff for the deck covering pure-asset coins, stablecoins, and CBDCs, and then strategy can take it forward from there.

turns.inner_thought: Good, that gives us Friday to sharpen the executive-briefing file in the strategy folder. When she says the deck, I assume she means the briefing deck we're already using. I need the latest version polished enough for Monday's prep so leadership can read it cold and not see any rough edges.
turns.utterance: Yes, that timing works for me. I'd just like the latest version of the deck ready for Monday's executive prep, with a clean narrative arc all the way through.

turns.inner_thought: The conceptual work is basically locked: taxonomy, monetary distinctions, and the balance-sheet treatment. We'll include the Bitcoin, stablecoin, and CBDC examples in the package as appendix support so the claims are fully sourced. That should satisfy any internal review standard without forcing us to rebuild the core story at the last minute.
turns.utterance: That should be fine. The core taxonomy and balance-sheet logic are locked now, and the balance-sheet examples for Bitcoin, stablecoins, and CBDCs will come over with the package.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect—that middle section needs those examples in the main flow or the room will blur the categories together. Executives won't go hunting in backup. If the examples are coming over, we can use them as the teaching device in the center of the story.
turns.utterance: Great. Those balance-sheet examples will be especially useful in the middle section, since executives need a simple way to distinguish the categories.

turns.inner_thought: As long as he owns the forward process after Thursday, that's exactly what I want. We'll hand over the content package and then stay available for factual checks, but I don't want my team line-editing slides in someone else's workflow all Friday.
turns.utterance: Exactly. Once research hands over on Thursday, strategy can take the deck forward, and my team will stay available for any factual questions that come up.

turns.inner_thought: Good—then we can move fast in the shared file. I'll have my associate tighten the headlines Friday morning and leave comments directly in the deck so research can answer or tweak wording in place. That should keep us from spinning up parallel versions.
turns.utterance: Sounds good. I'll have my associate tighten the headlines and leave comments directly so we can keep moving quickly on Friday.

turns.inner_thought: I should anchor what ready means in substance, not cosmetics. By Thursday, the claims themselves will be settled and sourced—reserve backing, issuer liabilities, non-liability coins. If that's clear, hopefully nobody expects a weekend-level design pass from research.
turns.utterance: And just so we're aligned, by Thursday the deck should be ready in the sense that the claims on reserve backing, issuer liabilities, and non-liability coins will all be fully substantiated.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, but I also need it to read cleanly for leadership. If there are placeholders, rough formatting, or side trips into technical detail, Monday gets messy. I assume she's saying the substance is locked and we'll have a presentation-ready flow by then.
turns.utterance: Agreed. And ready for me means leadership can read straight through without getting stuck on placeholders or technical detours.

turns.inner_thought: The deeper mechanics belong in backup, which is where those worked entries and the macro bridge sit. If leadership wants detail, it's there; otherwise the main deck can stay clean. I'm not hearing a need to reopen the core slides.
turns.utterance: Understood. The appendix will carry the worked balance-sheet entries and a macro-model bridge in case leadership wants to go deeper.

turns.inner_thought: Backup is fine, but the deck itself still needs those examples visible enough to do the explanatory work. If they're only buried in the appendix, we'll lose the room. I assume her latest deck already signals them clearly and we can build around that.
turns.utterance: That makes sense, as long as the deck itself still shows those examples clearly enough to anchor the story on how each crypto class functions economically.

turns.inner_thought: I'll send our latest research master and the support files by end of day Eastern on Thursday. That should conclude the handoff cleanly, and then strategy can proceed in its own lane. I really don't want a late-afternoon scramble over formatting requests.
turns.utterance: Perfect. I'll send the latest deck and the supporting files by end of day Thursday so strategy can proceed.

turns.inner_thought: I'll look for the updated strategy deck Thursday afternoon so we can spend Friday refining it. If that lands on time and it's truly ready, we should be in good shape for Monday with minimal cleanup from my team.
turns.utterance: Great, I'll look for that version Thursday afternoon, and if we stay on that timing, we should be in good shape for Monday.
